Legislative elections were held in [[Israel]] on 27 October 2026 to elect all 120 members of the [[26th Knesset]] and determine the governing coalition that succeeds the [[Thirty-seventh government of Israel|37th government]] led by Prime Minister [[Benjamin Netanyahu]].

The outgoing [[25th Knesset]] became the first Israeli legislature to complete its full four-year term without early dissolution since 1988, ending the prolonged [[2018–2022 Israeli political crisis|political crisis of 2018–2022]] that saw five consecutive snap elections. However, the government's tenure was marked by political turmoil, including [[2023 Israeli judicial reform protests|mass protests]] over [[2023 Israeli judicial reform|judicial reform]], the [[7 October attacks]] and the subsequent [[Gaza war]], and recurring coalition crises over [[Haredi conscription in Israel|Haredi military conscription]].

In this [[proportional representation]] system, parties must meet a 3.25% [[electoral threshold]] to enter the legislature.<ref name=nbc>{{cite web |title=High turnout in Israel’s election and Trump administration seeks to block alleged noncitizen votes: Morning Rundown |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/israel-election-netanyahu-trump-noncitizen-votes-morning-rundown-rcna605877 |website=NBC News |access-date=27 October 2026}}</ref>
